question: Which of the following sites is linked to the Indus Valley Civilisation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohenjo-Daro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro** is one of the major urban centers of the **Indus Valley Civilisation**, which is considered one of the world’s earliest urban civilizations.
 
• It is located in present-day **Sindh province of Pakistan** and was rediscovered in **1922** by archaeologist **R.D. Banerji**.
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro** is known for its advanced urban planning, including a **grid system layout**, sophisticated **drainage system**, and well-constructed residential and public buildings. *Hence, it is directly linked to the Indus Valley Civilisation.*
 
• Other sites like **Ajanta, Sanchi, and Bhimbetka** are significant for Indian history but belong to different historical periods and are not associated with the Indus Valley Civilisation.
 
• **Ajanta:** Known for its Buddhist cave paintings and sculptures, dating back to **2nd century BCE to 6th century CE**.
 
• **Sanchi:** Famous for its **Buddhist stupas**, especially the Great Stupa, constructed during Emperor **Ashoka’s reign** (3rd century BCE).
 
• **Bhimbetka:** Known for its rock shelters and cave paintings, which date back to the **Paleolithic and Mesolithic ages**.
 
• These sites are historically significant but are not connected to the Indus Valley Civilisation. *Hence, the correct answer is Mohenjo-Daro.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indus Valley Civilisation:**

 
 
• The **Indus Valley Civilisation** (also known as Harappan Civilisation) existed from approximately **3300 BCE to 1300 BCE**. It was primarily located in the northwestern regions of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The civilization is notable for its **urban planning, advanced drainage systems, standardized weights and measures, and trade networks.**
 
• Major sites include **Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan, and Rakhigarhi**.
 
 
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro:**
 
 
• The name **Mohenjo-Daro** translates to "**Mound of the Dead**" in Sindhi.
 
• Key features include the **Great Bath**, which is believed to have been used for ritualistic purposes, and the **Granary**, which indicates organized storage and trade.
 
• Artifacts like seals, beads, tools, and pottery found here provide insights into the life and culture of the Harappan people.
 
 
 
• **Other Sites:**
 
 
• **Ajanta:** Located in Maharashtra, it is renowned for its **Buddhist art** and cave architecture.
 
• **Sanchi:** Situated in Madhya Pradesh, it is a key site for Buddhist architectural heritage, particularly from the Mauryan Empire.
 
• **Bhimbetka:** Found in Madhya Pradesh, it houses prehistoric cave paintings and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **Rediscovery of Mohenjo-Daro:**

 
 
• Discovered in **1922** by **R.D. Banerji** during excavations led by the Archaeological Survey of India.
 
• It is one of the best-preserved urban sites of the **Indus Valley Civilisation**.
 
 
 
• **Decline of Indus Valley Civilisation:**
 
 
• Factors like **climate change, shifts in river courses, and possibly invasions** contributed to its decline around **1300 BCE**.
 
• However, the exact reasons for its decline remain a subject of ongoing research.
